For now, it's not clear if we can even get them or not!
An 11-year-old girl who lost her father in childhood lives with her mother and two school-age brothers in a home of less than 20 square meters. Her mother works in a sewing workshop to cover living expenses. On the eve of the new school year, her supplies for going to school were just a few pages from old drawing notebooks, some half-used pencils, and a blue pen... When we asked her, "What bag will you take to school this year?" she brought out a bag that had been donated to her in previous years; a bag whose torn parts her mother had repaired many times so her daughter could use the same bag for one more year. For some children, the start of the school year comes with buying a bag, notebooks, and pencils; but for this girl, even these few simple items are a dream.
Let's make the start of this school year sweeter for her and several other underprivileged students with a new bag and a few simple supplies.
The cost of each package for one student is 2,500,000 Toman.

.✍ Toto-chan
The book "The Dream School" is the true story of Toto-chan, a little Japanese girl, during her elementary school years. A little girl who later became a global figure. Why did she become a global figure? Because her mother didn't tell her until twenty years later that she had been expelled from school in that very first grade; she only said she wanted to take her to another school that she would love more. And that is the miraculous skill that many of us parents lack. This very "not saying" of one sentence completely changed Toto-chan's future, and it is because of not saying this one sentence that today the book Toto-chan holds the title of the best-selling book in Japan's history and has been translated into dozens of languages worldwide.
I won't tell you more than this, so you can read and hear it yourself. I have read this book once and listened to its audio version twice, and while reading this book, I cried several times for the injustice that goes on in the name of upbringing, at home and at school, against the children of my homeland. So definitely read or listen to it, even if you don't have children; and send it to anyone who has children or works with children: to fathers and mothers, to trainers, to teachers, and to anyone active in the field of childhood, education, and upbringing. Today (November 10th) has been designated by the United Nations as "World Science Day for Peace and Development." I am introducing this book today to remind that science by itself does not lead to peace and development. Science only serves peace and development when it is placed in the hands of humans who are enriched within and overflowing from without. And this enrichment and overflowing happen at home and at school. Toto-chan's story is the story of how a child is enriched internally and overflows externally. Toto-chan, the child of our story, is now ninety years old and is a UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador and an advisor to the World Wide Fund for Nature. You can also read its text at the link below. entry.summary:
Source: @yaser_arab57

♦️ Trees that become victims of war! ♦️📚@darvishnameh✍️ Mangroves, including Avicennia and Rhizophora species, help absorb carbon and produce oxygen several times more than any forest habitat we know, and in addition, they are highly effective in water bioremediation and aquatic spawning. But these days, the Qeshm mangrove habitat has become a victim of war, and its shores are covered in tar! We might think this tragedy ends with a few blackened trees! Not at all... that's not the story at all. What has happened is much bigger than a few trees burning and turning black. A mangrove is not just a tree. It's an ecosystem; a living network on which a large part of coastal and marine life depends. When oil enters this ecosystem, it doesn't just stick to the tree trunk; it enters a complete chain of life. And perhaps to understand the scale of this disaster, no explanation is as sufficient as seeing these images. This is not just oil pollution; part of an ecosystem is being buried under oil. An excerpt from the documentary "Qeshm Background Not" by Yaser Arab#Mangrove_Is_Irans_Life#Yaser_Arab #Mohammad_Darvish

What is presented here is the #KareKheir report for Mordad 1405, and it reaches you, dear ones, with the aim of letting you know how and where the funds you entrust to #KareKheir with various intentions have been spent. Furthermore, in Mordad, 9,732 deposits were made to the introduced accounts, which is about 600 more deposits than the previous month. Vital ConversationsMohammad FazeliFor a society that has experienced the bloody and catastrophic events of #Aban_98 (November 2019), dialogue about any plan related to changing gasoline and energy policy is vital. For a society where the #energy_imbalance has reached a life-or-death threshold, dialogue about any plan related to changing gasoline and energy policy is vital. A conversation with economist Dr. #Mohsen_Yazdanpanah, published on the IranTalk media platform under the title "Gasoline Reforms: Without Fireworks," was an attempt to open the door to dialogue about a plan some in the government are pursuing, critique it, and highlight its consequences.Watching "Gasoline Reforms: Without Fireworks" — any plan can be critiqued, including the current government's plan; and any critique can also be critiqued, including those Mohsen Yazdanpanah levels against the current plan. What matters is that for any chronic and complex issue — such as energy in today's Iran — there is no better path than policy transparency, social dialogue, and building social and political consensus around the best solutions. All those interested in energy policy discussions and debates on price and non-price reforms in gasoline and other energy carriers can be invited to watch this conversation and engage in the social debate about it. These are vital conversations. @fazeli_mohammad
